intro: Five villages and hamlets on the higher ground north of Evesham, all recorded in the Domesday Book. Church, Ab, Atch and Sheriffs Lench make up South Lenches parish; Rous Lench has its own parish council.

banner.alt: The Lenches villages in Worcestershire, seen from the air

villages.name: Church Lench
villages.text: The largest of the Lenches, with All Saints' church, the First School and Pre-school, the village hall, and the sports and members' clubs.

villages.name: Rous Lench
villages.text: Named after the Rous family, with the Grade I listed Norman church of St Peter, 16th-century Rous Lench Court and a village hall built in 1885.

villages.name: Ab Lench
villages.text: A hamlet west of Church Lench that shares All Saints' as its parish church.

villages.name: Atch Lench
villages.text: A hamlet south-east of Church Lench, whose red-brick Baptist chapel of 1829 is now a house.

villages.name: Sheriffs Lench
villages.text: A hamlet south-west of Church Lench, named after the Sheriffs of Worcestershire who held it for three centuries after the Norman Conquest.
